original.target_description: Study 1: dimensional Pearson correlation between dwell-time bias (negative minus non-negative faces) and overall anxiety symptom severity (average child/parent SCARED).

n.sample_role: Youth in post-exclusion dwell-time analyses: 28 anxiety patients and 22 healthy comparisons. Total 50 established from explicit initial sample and exclusions; not separately printed as N = 50.
n.exclusions: Four of 57 initially included youth excluded for insufficient data/aborting first run; three further influential outliers removed (2 healthy, 1 patient).

n.quote: a final sample of 53 youth (29 patients and 24 healthy comparisons; see Table 1). [...] Three outliers (2 healthy, 1 patient) were identified and removed from subsequent dwell-time analyses using this method

replication.target_description: Independent Abend et al. replication: correlation between dwell time bias-score and overall anxiety symptom severity; excludes combined-sample correlation.

n.sample_role: Youth with dwell bias-score and overall anxiety symptom severity measurements; exact analytic N not explicitly supplied for this correlation.
n.exclusions: Four outliers removed for preceding mixed model (N = 105). Correlation is printed as r(104); paper does not explicitly reconcile its sample with either N = 109 or N = 105. No generic N substituted.
n.location: p. 4, Results, Independent replication samples, Abend et al. [14], first paragraph
n.quote: the correlation analysis between dwell time bias-score and overall anxiety symptom severity was not significant, r(104) = -0.03, p = .74.

notes: Original analytic N = 50 follows the explicit 53-person sample minus three exclusions and agrees with printed r(48). Replication analytic N left null because the correlation r(104) is not explicitly reconciled with the reported independent samples of 109 before and 105 after mixed-model exclusions. No N inferred from r degrees of freedom. Supplied p. 7 locator interpreted as Study 1 symptom correlation, supported by the exact corresponding replication analysis.
